title: Hummingbird Cake
summary: A moist, spiced Southern-style layer cake built on banana, pineapple and toasted pecans, stacked with cream cheese frosting between the layers.
equipment: three 20 cm round cake tins (5 cm deep), greased and base-lined
stand mixer or electric hand whisk

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
tinned crushed pineapple in juice, undrained (1 small tin)
pecans, toasted and chopped, plus 12 halves to decorate
full-fat cream cheese (block), at room temperature
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Preheat the oven
steps.text: Heat the oven to 175°C (155°C fan) with a shelf in the middle (or two, staggered, if needed), giving it at least 20 minutes to reach temperature before baking three cake layers.

steps.title: Toast the pecans
steps.text: Spread all the pecans on a tray and toast for 8 minutes, until fragrant, then leave to cool before chopping all but the 12 halves set aside for decoration. Toasting first brings out more of their flavour than adding them raw.

steps.title: Mix wet and dry separately
steps.text: Whisk the flour, bicarbonate of soda, cinnamon and salt together in one bowl. In another, whisk the eggs and sugar, then stir in the oil and vanilla, followed by the mashed banana and the tinned pineapple with its juice.

steps.title: Combine gently
steps.text: Stir the dry mixture into the wet ingredients just until no flour is visible, then fold in the chopped pecans. Don't beat the batter here – a light hand is what keeps this dense, fruit-packed crumb tender rather than heavy.

steps.title: Bake the layers
steps.text: Divide the batter evenly between the three tins and bake for 25-30 minutes, until golden and a skewer inserted into the centre comes out clean. Cool in the tins for 10 minutes, then turn out and leave to cool completely on a rack.

steps.title: Make the cream cheese frosting
steps.text: Beat the butter until smooth, then add the cream cheese and beat only until combined, since overbeating it makes the frosting too soft to hold its shape. Mix in the icing sugar, vanilla and salt on low speed until smooth, chilling for 15 minutes if it feels soft.

steps.title: Stack and frost
steps.text: Stack the three cooled layers with a generous layer of frosting between each, then spread the rest over the top and sides with a palette knife. Press the reserved pecan halves around the top to decorate.

steps.title: Chill and serve
steps.text: Keep the cake in the fridge until ready to serve, then let it sit out briefly to come back towards room temperature – this softens the frosting and brings the spices back into focus.

tips: Stir the batter only until no flour is visible once the wet and dry mixtures meet – overmixing knocks out air and makes the dense banana-pineapple crumb heavy rather than moist.
Toast the pecans and let them cool before chopping, since warm nuts release oil that can make the batter greasy.
Beat the cream cheese frosting only until combined, not longer, or it turns soft and difficult to spread neatly.
Let all three layers cool completely before stacking and frosting, or the layers can slide out of line.
Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Keep the frosted cake in the fridge, loosely covered, for up to 4 days, bringing slices back towards room temperature before serving. Unfrosted sponge layers freeze well, wrapped tightly, for up to 2 months.
